Jane (Acme): Hey @support — we're seeing intermittent failures on streaming responses to our users. Starts around 2026-03-15 06:10 UTC. Client reports truncated responses and our billing shows a big uptick of 5xx hits for the /v1/stream endpoint. Can provide request ids and a short video.

Elena Park: Thanks Jane — sorry about that. Can you paste one of the request ids and approximate timestamps? Did the client abort, or did they get an HTTP error?

Jane (Acme): Request ids: r-8f3b6c (06:11:02), r-8f3b9a (06:13:44). The client sees a network error in the UI; server side shows a 502 logged and the response truncated mid-chunk. The SDK did not explicitly call abort.

Ravi Patel: Jumping in — @Elena can you add logs? Do we have gateway logs or runtime stack traces for those request ids?

OpsBot: Alert: spike in gateway 5xx for /v1/stream between 06:09–06:16 UTC. Count: +412 vs baseline 12.

Elena Park: Pasted logs for r-8f3b6c below (sanitized):

```
[gateway] 2026-03-15T06:11:02.213Z INFO req=r-8f3b6c client_ip=54.12.23.1 method=POST path=/v1/stream status=502 upstream_status=200 bytes_sent=1024 user_agent="acme-sdk/1.2"
[runtime] 2026-03-15T06:11:02.214Z ERROR req=r-8f3b6c write failed: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->54.12.23.1:52110: write: broken pipe
[upstream] 2026-03-15T06:11:02.215Z INFO req=r-8f3b6c model=redwood-ggml chunk_sent=true
```

Theo Nguyen: Hmm write failed + gateway logged 502 while upstream had status=200 and chunk_sent=true. That implies upstream started streaming, we wrote at least one chunk, then the socket write failed (SIGPIPE / EPIPE) and gateway classified it as 5xx.

Ben SRE: This matches a known ambiguity in our gateway classification: if an ECONNRESET or EPIPE happens after we've already flushed chunked data, we sometimes attribute it to upstream (5xx) instead of client abort. Billing/monitoring then counts that as server error.

Elena Park: Are there repro steps we can give Acme so they can confirm it's client-side abort? Or should we reproduce internally?

Ravi Patel: I'll try to reproduce with a small script that opens a streaming request, receives one chunk, then closes the socket without finishing. Use this curl-ish demo:

```
# PoC: open streaming request, read 1 chunk, then close connection
python - <<'PY'
import socket, ssl, time
s = socket.create_connection(("api.redwood.ai", 443))
s = ssl.wrap_socket(s)
req = "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nAuthorization: Bearer REDACT\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n1\r\n{\n\r\n}\r\n0\r\n\r\n"
s.send(req.encode())
# read a bit, then drop socket abruptly
time.sleep(0.5)
s.close()
PY
```

Theo Nguyen: Nice. I reproduced locally — gateway shows same pattern: upstream sends initial chunks (200 partial), then socket closed by client => gateway logs 502 + write failed: broken pipe.

Ben SRE: Root cause hypothesis: classification logic in our gateway assumes any write error during response streaming is an upstream failure unless the client sent a FIN prior to first write. But in chunked transfer the client can tear down socket after receiving a chunk; kernel reports EPIPE on the write to client and our metric mapper records a 5xx.

Elena Park: Proposed mitigation: change metric classifier to check whether upstream already sent a 2xx partial AND whether client closed connection (detect via ECONNRESET timing), then attribute to client abort (4xx-like). Short term we can roll a config switch to treat EPIPE after first-chunk as client abort for billing windows.

Ravi Patel: I've got a hotfix branch: gateway: feature/stream-disconnect-classify-client. It toggles the behavior with env STREAM_DISCONNECT_AS_CLIENT=true. Would like to test in staging then can roll to prod traffic via canary.

Ben SRE: Also file for billing: support will mark affected request ids as non-billable and we need to credit customers for 06:09–06:17 UTC. @billing FYI.

Elena Park: Repro steps for SRE / QA: 1) run PoC python above; 2) tail gateway logs for req id; 3) confirm log sequence: upstream chunk -> write failed EPIPE -> gateway 502. If hotfix is on, classifier should emit: client_abort=true and metric should be classified as client_disconnect (not 5xx).

OpsBot: Deploy pipeline started for feature/stream-disconnect-classify-client -> staging (build 2026-03-15T07:02).

Ravi Patel: Quick test on staging: toggled STREAM_DISCONNECT_AS_CLIENT=true, ran PoC, gateway logs now: 
```
[gateway] ... req=r-xxxxx client_abort=true classification=client_disconnect
[metrics] req=r-xxxxx counted=client_disconnect
```
Works as expected.

Jane (Acme): Thanks — do you have ETA for prod roll? Our customers are very upset about the billing hits.

Elena Park: Planning canary tomorrow morning 07:30 UTC, then ramp to 50% and full in 2 hours if metrics look good. We'll proactively credit the impacted invoices for Acme for the 06:09–06:17 window. I'll confirm once canary passes.

Ben SRE: Follow-up action items:
- [Elena] Confirm billing credits and notify Acme.
- [Ravi] Push hotfix to staging -> prod canary and monitor 5xx spike.
- [Theo] Add unit/integration tests for chunked EPIPE classification.
- [Billing] Prepare credit for affected accounts.

Elena Park: Thanks all :thumbsup: Jane — we'll update you in this thread when the canary completes and when billing is done.

Ravi Patel: Canary looked good. Rolling to 100% at 07:45 UTC.
